I spoke with Emma Vigeland for the Majority Report recently about the concerning rise in ICE detention camp deaths this year. Tune in below.  

piped.video/watch?v=zbeh29jz…

The numbers are stark, but numbers alone don't capture what's at stake. These are people with lives, families, and legal rights. 

Read: nbcnews.com/news/us-news/arr…

For deeper analysis visit: austinkocher.substack.com 

Full Report: deportationdata.org/analysis…
Deportations of people already living in the U.S. (not border crossers) increased fivefold. Detention beds for interior arrests more than quadrupled.

The enforcement surge isn't limited to Democratic cities. At the peak of the Minneapolis operation, those arrests were only 15% of national street arrests. This expansion is, in the words of the researchers, "truly national."
Detention is doing policy work here. The report found that even people who likely could win their cases are being deported because prolonged detention causes people to abandon their legal claims.

The administration says 70% of its arrests are of people with criminal records. The data says otherwise. ICE's own records (obtained through a FOIA lawsuit) show the agency is "much less likely to target people with criminal convictions" than before.

ICE street arrests are arrests outside of jails and prisons, in communities. The Deportation Data Project calls this scale "a new phenomenon." It signals a fundamental shift from criminal-justice-based enforcement to population-wide enforcement.

A new UC Berkeley analysis found ICE arrests of people with no criminal record surged 770% in Trump's first year back. Street arrests (in neighborhoods, at courthouses, at check-ins) jumped over 1,000%. Here's what it means. 🧵

A woman who experienced a miscarriage in detention received no medical care for 10 days, was deported in an acute medical crisis, and had her life saved only because reception center workers in Honduras rushed her to an emergency room. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…�

Video

Aled Damien Carbonell-Betancourt is the 17th Reported ICE Detention Death of 2026

A 27-year-old man from Cuba died on April 12, one day after the 16th death of the year. The pace of detention deaths holds at an average of 1 every 6 days. 

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

I live in Baltimore, so it was a big deal to me when the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapsed, killing several immigrant workers. Adding injury to injury, the mother of one of those men, Guerra Sandoval, is facing deportation. Our country is broken.

wxpr.org/2026-04-24/dhs-star…
The full breakdown of the Tobay Robles case, the history of habeas corpus, and what a de facto suspension of due process looks like in practice is here: austinkocher.substack.com/p/…
What the data doesn't yet tell us: how often courts are actually enforcing these orders versus issuing them and moving on. Contempt threats are meaningful but only if they're followed through.

I saw a similar spike in habeas cases at the start of COVID-19, when ICE detention centers became dangerous infection sites. The mechanism is the same: a surge in enforcement without legal safeguards forces people into court. This spike is larger.

In the Minnesota case, Judge Patrick Schiltz took the U.S. Attorney to task for what he described as an embarrassing response to court concerns. When judges appointed by Republican presidents threaten contempt, that tells you something.

Habeas corpus is the legal mechanism that lets people challenge whether their detention is lawful. It's in Article 1 of the Constitution. The administration has openly discussed suspending it and may not need to if agencies can simply ignore court orders.
A federal judge in Minnesota threatened criminal contempt against the U.S. Attorney's office for ignoring a habeas corpus order in an ICE detention case.

It’s like they never even heard of January 6.


John the Cliff Dweller (@STFUabtChicago)

So, am I to understand that a student teacher from California was able to travel to DC, book a room at the same venue and on the same night as the WHCD, and occupy the room without having his luggage searched?



— https://nitter.net/STFUabtChicago/status/2048382290326114649#m
